arguments.brief: Build a simple responsive tide app. Let me choose a coastal location and day, see the tide height and whether it is rising or falling, the next high and low tides, and a readable 24-hour tide chart. Use the supplied data.

activity_model.activity: Check tides for a coastal outing.
activity_model.objective: Understand tide conditions for a chosen coastal location and day.
outcomes: Read noon height and direction, next high and low tides and the full day curve.
tools_and_artifacts: Supplied tide readings and daily events
rules_and_rituals: Use Pacific time and metres; reference noon on the chosen day.
division_of_labor: Person selects place and day; app calculates and presents supplied tide information.

interaction_contract.primary_decision: Which location and day to inspect?
next_actions: Compare upcoming high and low tides with the day curve
meaningful_state_changes: Location/day selection changes all measurements and chart scale together.
interaction_contract.completion: The person can read the selected day tide height, direction, upcoming events, and 24-hour pattern.
make_easy: Keep selections and resulting values visible together.

boundaries: Information from supplied values; no activity suitability decision is made.

assumptions.statement: Single informational view rather than an outing booking or safety decision.

context_items.content: Use the supplied React 19 / esbuild starter and unchanged public/data.js. The shared fixture contains 14 coastal locations and two dates. Measurements are metres and times Pacific time; the clock is noon on the selected day. Initial selection is Half Moon Bay, 2026-10-06. Every location/day must update all readings and the chart from the supplied values, with a chart scale that contains the selected data. Build and check with npm run build and npm run check. dist/index.html must work by file and local HTTP. Desktop 1280x800, mobile 390x844. Use local assets and system fonts; no live data APIs. Design decisions are delegated. Show light mode only with no system-theme switching. Do not add demo-data banners or notices. Keep units, timezone and selected-day clock clear. Output working code and RUN.md with resource calls, outcomes, QA, assumptions, and limitations. Standard file/shell/browser infrastructure is common to all conditions.
